research_question: What is the effect of psychosocial interventions compared with an inactive control on PTSD symptom severity immediately after treatment in adults who have experienced rape or sexual assault?
control_label: Inactive control (wait-list, usual care, or assessment only)
outcome_description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptom severity measured on a continuous validated scale (clinician-administered like CAPS or primary self-report like PDS, PCL, PSS-SR, IES-R) immediately after treatment completion.
positive_direction: Greater reduction in PTSD symptom severity (fewer PTSD symptoms) favoring the psychosocial intervention over inactive control
search_queries: psychosocial intervention PTSD sexual assault trial
cognitive behavioral therapy rape PTSD controlled trial
prolonged exposure sexual assault PTSD randomized outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating psychosocial interventions (including CBT, prolonged exposure, CPT, stress inoculation, EMDR, narrative exposure, or brief/computerised programmes) compared with an inactive control (wait-list, treatment as usual, no treatment, or assessment only).
Adults (aged 18 or older) who have experienced rape or sexual assault in adulthood.
Quantitative continuous assessment of PTSD symptom severity measured immediately post-treatment on a validated scale.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocol papers, editorials, qualitative studies, or theoretical papers).
Non-randomised studies or trials comparing active interventions without an inactive control condition.
Studies focusing exclusively on childhood sexual abuse, military or combat trauma without adult sexual assault, or non-adult populations (<18 years).
Absence of quantitative post-treatment PTSD outcome data sufficient to calculate an effect size (e.g., missing means, SDs, sample sizes, or test statistics).
moderators_to_extract: Intervention type (e.g., prolonged exposure, CBT, CPT, EMDR, brief/digital)
Control condition type (wait-list, usual care, assessment only, no treatment)
Outcome measurement type (clinician-administered interview vs self-report scale)
Number of intervention sessions or treatment duration
effect_size_note: Post-treatment PTSD symptom scores pooled as standardised mean difference (SMD, Hedges' g) using a random-effects model. With higher_score_is_worse set to True, positive effect sizes represent greater symptom reduction favoring the psychosocial intervention. Extract end-of-treatment values using clinician-administered scales preferentially, or primary self-report total scores. Multi-arm trials split control sample size across active comparisons.
